title: Binary classification: what its pitfalls cost on its replica
question: On the Binary classification replica, how much better does a wrong split or a kept leak make the score look?
setup_summary: 3 seeds of the binary replica; 20% held out; histogram gradient boosting with default settings; ROC-AUC; right split: the latest rows by time.

claims.statement: On the Binary classification replica, a random split instead of the latest rows by time showed no difference beyond the spread of 3 seeds (mean 0.0062, 95% interval -0.0315 to 0.0438).
limitations: Invented replica data with its traps planted, one model family with default settings: the size of the effect on a real table differs; the direction is what the replica shows.

No difference measured on this replica: it plants no effect of this kind (no drift over time), which says nothing about a real table, where a random split is still the wrong one for a time-ordered problem.

claims.statement: On the Binary classification replica, the planted leak kept in makes the ROC-AUC look better by 0.3361 on average over 3 seeds (95% interval 0.2916 to 0.3806).
limitations: Invented replica data with its traps planted, one model family with default settings: the size of the effect on a real table differs; the direction is what the replica shows.
